issue.body_html:
it is generally recommended that on 503, if the server responds with the Retry-After header we should respect that and if it's not present we should default back exponential backoff.

Is this something that coud be considered to be added directly into the RetryClient, so we have that as default behaviour?

I am asking this because we already retrying 503 by default.

issue.body:
it is generally recommended that on 503, if the server responds with the `Retry-After` header we should respect that and if it's not present we should default back exponential backoff.

Is this something that coud be considered to be added directly into the `RetryClient`, so we have that as default behaviour?

I am asking this because we already retrying [503 by default](https://github.com/dart-lang/http/blob/2cb6c12966e18abc11a0217a8b613742849a29ea/pkgs/http/lib/retry.dart#L182C1-L182C4).

The most obvious way of doing this is to make `BaseResponse` available in the `delay` function. But that would be a breaking change.

comments.body_html:
Another way to do this without breaking the existing API is to keep delay(int retryCount) as the default backoff policy and add a separate opt-in callback for response-aware delays. For example:

Duration? Function(BaseResponse response, int retryCount)? retryDelay

The default implementation would continue using the current exponential backoff, while callers that need server-controlled retry timing can provide a function that reads Retry-After and returns the appropriate delay. This preserves compatibility for existing users while allowing Retry-After support without changing the meaning of delay.
That keeps the change focused and avoids forcing all retry users to depend on BaseResponse in the existing callback.

nodes.title: Add retryDelay callback to RetryClient to support Retry-After header

issue.title: Add retryDelay callback to RetryClient to support Retry-After header
issue.body_html:
Adds an optional retryDelay callback to RetryClient that receives the
BaseResponse and the zero-based retry count, and may return a Duration to
use as the wait time for that retry attempt.

This is a strictly additive, non-breaking change. The existing delay callback
and all other constructor parameters are completely unchanged.

Solution

Keep delay(int retryCount) as-is and add a separate opt-in callback:

Duration? Function(BaseResponse response, int retryCount)? retryDelay

When retryDelay is provided and returns a non-null Duration, that value is
used as the wait time. When it returns null (or is not provided), the existing
delay callback is used as the fallback. Example usage for honouring
Retry-After:

final client = RetryClient(
  Client(),
  retryDelay: (response, retryCount) {
    final retryAfter = response.headers['retry-after'];
    if (retryAfter != null) {
      final seconds = int.tryParse(retryAfter);
      if (seconds != null) return Duration(seconds: seconds);
    }
    return null; // fall back to exponential backoff
  },
);

Changes

  • pkgs/http/lib/retry.dart — new _retryDelay field, new retryDelay
    constructor parameter, updated delay computation in send()
  • pkgs/http/test/http_retry_test.dart — two new tests: fix-checking
    (retryDelay callback is used when Retry-After header is present) and
    preservation (retryDelay returning null falls back to delay callback)
  • pkgs/http/CHANGELOG.md — entry added under 1.7.0-wip

Fixes #1841

  • I've reviewed the contributor guide and applied the relevant portions to this PR.
